productQualityProblem: Joy contributes 24 historical false positives, while sadness is another frequent short-domain output. Product-18 pseudo-label distillation sharpened teacher biases and increased false positives. A non-categorical auxiliary signal is needed to expose the encoder to short event affect without manufacturing Product-18 gold.
hypothesis: Training only the incumbent's top two encoder layers on the rights-cleared native human positive/negative/neither valence task from Unexpected Events, with a separate temporary valence head and the Product-18 classifier head frozen, may improve short-event affect representations without reinforcing categorical pseudo-label errors.

data.admission: ADMIT_UNLABELED for Product-18; native valence is human source-task supervision but NOT Product-18 gold
data.labels: best_senti for experiments 1/2 and val_code for experiment 3; pos/neg/neither only
data.forbiddenMapping: Valence classes must not be converted into Product-18 labels
data.leakage: Use existing participant-disjoint train/validation split; fit only on train

fixedTraining.runtimeLengthNote: 512 tokens is safety only; every selected text is complete and <=300 characters
fixedTraining.updates: top two encoder layers plus temporary 3-class valence head
fixedTraining.emotionClassifierHead: frozen byte-identical; temporary valence head discarded
fixedTraining.loss: train-derived square-root inverse-frequency weighted cross entropy
fixedTraining.sampling: deterministic shuffle; no source or label sweep

successCriteria.historicalDevelopment: emotion micro-F1 >=0.528052805280528, false positives <=58, false negatives <=85, and no supported-label F1 regression worse than 0.05
successCriteria.shortDevelopmentSlice: false positives <=5 and micro-F1 regression no worse than 0.02; descriptive guard only
successCriteria.unlabeledBehavior: Hippocorpus exact-output agreement with incumbent >=0.85; both validation sources have each 0/1/2 distribution shift <=0.08 absolute
successCriteria.decision: RETAIN_FOR_RESEARCH only if every criterion passes; otherwise REJECT
